5. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common styles of Victorian-era vases include Orientalism, Rococo Revival, Neo-Classicism, Aesthetic Movement, and Art Nouveau.
6. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Decoration techniques for Victorian-era vases included transfer printing, hand-painting, gilding, and enamelwork.

9. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Aesthetic Movement emphasized beauty, taste, and sensuality, reacting against strict Victorian values.
10. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common motifs in the Aesthetic Movement included florals, birds, foliage, insects, geometric patterns, Asian influences, gilding, and whiplash curves.
11. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user was advised to look for ornate decoration, floral motifs, birds, insects, geometric patterns, Asian influences, luxurious materials, and whiplash curves to identify Aesthetic Movement designs on their vase.
12. [USER] The user expressed interest in learning more about the Art Nouveau style and how it differs from the Aesthetic Movement.
13. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Art Nouveau emerged around 1890-1910 and was characterized by organic forms, sinuous lines, whiplash motifs, and nature inspiration.
14. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Art Nouveau was more radical and experimental than the Aesthetic Movement, with a greater emphasis on line and form and less focus on decoration.
15. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user was advised to look for organic forms, sinuous lines, whiplash motifs, and innovative materials to identify Art Nouveau designs on their vase.
